mainTopic: Hidden dangers (זוגות, שדים, כשפים) and their limits and remedies
overview: This amud opens at the end of a discussion about זוגות, the danger of drinking an even number of cups. An earlier view says that water mixed into water does not count as a new cup. רבי יוחנן says it does count, and רב פפא limits that to hot water mixed with cold. Next, ריש לקיש lists four actions that put a person in danger: relieving oneself between a palm tree and a wall, passing between two palm trees, drinking borrowed water, and walking over spilled water. Using the formula 'לא אמרן אלא', the גמרא narrows each case step by step. It then warns that these leniencies do not help where there is a real threat of כשפים, and tells a story to prove it. A ברייתא lists things that should not pass between two people, and the גמרא gives remedies: reciting פסוקים that begin and end with אל or with לא. It adds more dangers with their fixes: a נדה passing between two men, two women doing כשפים at a crossroads, and meeting a woman coming up from her טבילת מצוה. Finally, רבי יצחק reads 'גיא צלמות' as sleeping in the shadow of a lone palm tree or of the moon, and the גמרא defines when each of these is dangerous.

steps.title: Mixing counts toward pairs, except water
steps.stepSummary: This is the tail end of a ruling from the previous daf: diluted drinks count toward זוגות, except when water is mixed with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement it began on the previous daf. A drink that was diluted counts as a separate cup toward the danger of זוגות, but water mixed into water does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether mixing one liquid into another turns it into a 'new' cup for the count of pairs. The earlier view says that mixing does count, with one exception: water poured into water stays plain water and adds nothing to the count.

keyTerms.meaning: pairs; the danger of drinking an even number of cups

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling standing on its own. It is the last words of a statement from the previous daf, so read it as 'everything counts, except water.'

phrases.english: Except for water.
phrases.notes: Water mixed with water does not count as a new cup toward pairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מִן הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed drinks count toward זוגות, except water mixed with water.

steps.title: Even water mixed with water counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and holds that even water mixed with water counts toward זוגות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: even water counts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with the exception in the previous step. In his view, even water mixed with water counts as a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view treated water as an exception, and רבי יוחנן removes that exception. For him, mixing water also creates a new cup in the count of pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: a leading אמורא of the Land of Israel

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even water.
phrases.notes: Even water mixed with water counts toward pairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the exception made for water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water mixed with water also counts toward זוגות.

steps.title: Only hot water mixed with cold counts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits רבי יוחנן's view: it applies only to hot water mixed with cold or cold mixed with hot, not to same-temperature water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: we said this only about hot water poured into cold or cold poured into hot. But hot into hot, or cold into cold, does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows רבי יוחנן's ruling. Water counts as 'mixed' only when the temperatures are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot and cold water change each other, so the result is a truly new drink. Water of the same temperature does not change at all, so everyone agrees it is not a new cup. רבי יוחנן's argument with the earlier view is therefore limited to the hot-and-cold case.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when (a formula that limits a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, water counts toward זוגות only when hot is mixed with cold, which is when the drink actually changes.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We said this only
hot water into cold,
and cold water into hot.
But hot into hot,
and cold into cold, no.
phrases.notes: These do not count as diluted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only water of different temperatures counts as a mixture toward זוגות.

steps.title: Four actions that endanger a person
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש lists four actions that put the person's life in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: there are four things that, if a person does them, his blood is on his own head and he endangers his life. These are: relieving oneself between a palm tree and a wall, passing between two palm trees, drinking borrowed water, and passing over spilled water, even if his wife poured it out in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new list of dangerous actions. It continues the general theme of hidden dangers, such as harmful spirits, from the discussion of זוגות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש names four specific actions. 'His blood is on his own head' means that if harm comes to him, he brought it on himself. The four cases will be explained and narrowed one at a time in the steps that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: his blood is on his own head; he is responsible for his own harm

steps.confusionAlert: Even the case where his own wife spilled the water in front of him is included. Knowing who spilled it does not remove the danger.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Four things, one who does them,
his blood is on his head and he is liable with his life.
These are they:
one who relieves himself between a palm tree and a wall,
and one who passes between two palm trees,
and one who drinks borrowed water,
and one who passes over spilled water,
even if his wife spilled it in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new list of dangers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four actions put a person in danger, and he is responsible for any harm that results.

steps.title: Palm tree and wall: only if less than four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The danger between a palm tree and a wall applies only when the gap is less than ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Relieving oneself between a palm tree and a wall: we said this only when there are not four cubits of space. If there are four cubits, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts narrowing the first case on ריש לקיש's list. The danger exists only in a narrow gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the person blocks the path of שדים (harmful spirits). If the space is ארבע אמות or more, there is enough room for them to pass, so there is no danger.

keyTerms.meaning: we have no problem with it

phrases.english: One who relieves himself between a palm tree and a wall:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: we said this only when it does not have four cubits,
but if it has four cubits,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנִּפְנֶה בֵּין דֶּקֶל לְכוֹתֶל — לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the first case on the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger applies only when the gap is less than four cubits.

steps.title: Narrow gap: only if there is no other route
steps.stepSummary: Even when the gap is narrow, the danger applies only when there is no other path.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when there are not four cubits, we said this only when there is no other route. If there is another route, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit on top of the first. Even a narrow gap is dangerous only when it is the only path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שדים can go another way, the person is not really blocking them. So the danger requires two conditions together: a gap of less than ארבע אמות, and no other route.
steps.whatToRemember: The palm-tree-and-wall danger requires both a gap of less than four cubits and no other route.

phrases.english: And when it does not have four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא דִּירְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: we said this only when there is no other route,
but if there is another route,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֵית לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, further limit to the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A narrow gap is dangerous only when there is no other route.

steps.title: Two palm trees: only if no public domain separates them
steps.stepSummary: Passing between two palm trees is dangerous only when no public road runs between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who passes between two palm trees: we said this only when a public domain does not cut between them. If a public domain cuts between them, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the second case on ריש לקיש's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שדים are not permitted to cause harm in a public place. So if a רשות הרבים crosses between the trees, passing there is not dangerous.

phrases.english: And one who passes between two palm trees:
we said this only
when a public domain does not cut between them,
but if a public domain cuts between them,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָעוֹבֵר בֵּין שְׁנֵי דְקָלִים — לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to narrowing the second case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger applies only when no public domain separates the trees.

steps.title: Borrowed water: only if a minor borrowed it
steps.stepSummary: Drinking borrowed water is dangerous only when a קטן borrowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who drinks borrowed water: we said this only when a minor borrowed it. But if an adult borrowed it, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the third case on ריש לקיש's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger depends on who borrowed the water. If a קטן borrowed it, there is danger. If a גדול borrowed it, there is none. The next two steps add more limits to this same case before the גמרא reaches the fourth case, spilled water.

phrases.english: One who drinks borrowed water:
we said this only when a minor borrowed it,
but an adult,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹתֶה מַיִם שְׁאוּלִין — לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to narrowing the third case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowed water is dangerous only when a minor borrowed it.

steps.title: Borrowed water is a danger only in a field
steps.stepSummary: Even when a קטן borrowed the water, the danger applies only in a field, where water is scarce, and not in a city, where water is common.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when a minor borrowed it, we only said this about a field, where water is not common. But in a city, where water is common, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps narrowing the danger of drinking borrowed water. It now limits it to a field, not a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 already limited the danger to water borrowed by a קטן. Now a second condition is added: it must be in a field. In a city water is easy to find, so the special worry does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when... (a limiting formula)
we have no problem with it

steps.confusionAlert: Each new 'לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא' adds one more condition on top of the earlier ones. The danger keeps getting smaller. The גמרא is not starting over each time.

phrases.english: And even if a minor borrowed it,
we only said this in a field,
where water is not common,
but in a city, where water is common,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ שַׁיְילִינְהוּ קָטָן נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limiting condition (field, not city) to Step 8's limit about a קטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger of borrowed water applies only in a field, where water is scarce, and not in a city.

steps.title: Only water, not wine or beer
steps.stepSummary: Even in a field, the danger applies only to borrowed water, not to borrowed wine or beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even in a field, we only said this about water. But wine and beer, we have no problem with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more limit: the danger is only with water. Borrowed wine or beer is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the danger needs three things together: a קטן borrowed it, in a field, and it is water. Wine and beer are left out completely.
steps.whatToRemember: Borrowed drink is a danger only if all three are true: a קטן borrowed it, it happened in a field, and it is water.

phrases.english: And even in a field,
we only said this about water,
but wine and beer,
we have no problem with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last limiting condition on borrowed drink (water only).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowed wine and beer carry no danger. Only water does.

steps.title: Spilled water is safe if covered with dirt or spat on
steps.stepSummary: Walking over spilled water is dangerous only if nobody put dirt on it or spat in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who walks over spilled water: we only said it is dangerous when it was not broken up with dirt and no one spat in it. But if it was broken up with dirt or someone spat in it, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on ריש לקיש's list, walking over spilled water. It starts narrowing that danger too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the water with dirt or spitting in it cancels the danger. Only one of these is needed ('אוֹ', or) to make it safe.

phrases.english: And one who passes over spilled water,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַפְסְקִינְהוּ בְּעַפְרָא
phrases.english: we only said this when no one covered it with dirt
and no one spat in it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַפְסְקִינְהוּ אוֹ תַּף בְּהוּ רוּקָּא —
phrases.english: but if someone covered it or spat in it,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָעוֹבֵר עַל מַיִם שְׁפוּכִין לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes with borrowed water and turns to a new item from ריש לקיש's list in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spilled water that was covered with dirt or spat in is not dangerous to walk over.

steps.title: Sun and sixty footsteps cancel the danger
steps.stepSummary: The danger of spilled water applies only if the sun has not passed over it and sixty footsteps have not passed over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when the sun did not pass over it and sixty footsteps did not pass over it. But if the sun passed over it and sixty footsteps passed over it, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another condition for the danger of spilled water. Sunlight together with sixty footsteps makes it safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both things are needed together ('וַעֲבַר', and). Only when the sun has passed over the water and sixty steps have crossed it is the danger gone.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא עֲבַר עֲלַיְיהוּ שִׁימְשָׁא
phrases.english: And we only said this when the sun did not pass over it
and sixty steps did not pass over it,
but if the sun passed over it
and sixty steps passed over it,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא עֲבַר עֲלַיְיהוּ שִׁימְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limiting condition on spilled water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spilled water that the sun and sixty footsteps have passed over is not dangerous.

steps.title: Riding a donkey and wearing shoes protects
steps.stepSummary: The danger of spilled water applies only to someone on foot without shoes. A person riding a donkey and wearing shoes is safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when he was not riding a donkey and not wearing shoes. But if he was riding a donkey and wearing shoes, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third condition about the person himself. If he is riding and wearing shoes, the spilled water does not harm him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier conditions were about the water itself. This one is about the person crossing it: riding a donkey and wearing shoes protect him.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא רְכִיב חֲמָרָא
phrases.english: And we only said this when he was not riding a donkey
and not wearing shoes,
but if he was riding a donkey and wearing shoes,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא רְכִיב חֲמָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third limiting condition, this time about the person rather than the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone riding a donkey and wearing shoes may cross spilled water without concern.

steps.title: Where witchcraft is a real concern, the leniencies do not help
steps.stepSummary: All these leniencies apply only where there is no reason to fear כשפים. Where there is, we are concerned even if all the safe conditions are present.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these words apply only where there is no reason to fear witchcraft. But where there is reason to fear witchcraft, even if all these conditions are present, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a big limit on all the leniencies it just gave. If someone might really be trying to harm you with כשפים, none of them protect you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-13 listed ways the danger of spilled water goes away. This step says those ways work only in the normal case. When there is a real threat of כשפים (for example, someone who wants to hurt this person), we still worry.
steps.whatToRemember: The safety conditions (dirt, spit, sun and sixty steps, donkey and shoes) work only when there is no real threat of כשפים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that all the leniencies are about ordinary risk. They do not cancel a deliberate threat.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ לִכְשָׁפִים,
phrases.english: And these words apply where there is no concern for witchcraft,
but where there is concern for witchcraft,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא כׇּל הָנֵי —
phrases.english: even though all these conditions are present,
we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ לִכְשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits all the leniencies of Steps 11-13 to cases with no real threat of כשפים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where there is a real concern of כשפים, we are concerned even when all the protective conditions are present.

steps.title: The man whose shoes and feet shriveled
steps.stepSummary: A story: a man who was riding a donkey and wearing shoes crossed water anyway, and his shoes shrank and his feet shriveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a certain man who was riding a donkey and wearing shoes, and his shoes shrank and his feet shriveled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short story that shows the rule from the step before in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man had the protection from Step 13: riding a donkey and wearing shoes. He was still harmed, which shows that when כשפים are aimed at someone, the usual protections do not work.

phrases.english: And a certain man who was riding a donkey
and wearing shoes,
and his shoes shrank
and his feet shriveled up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּרְכִיב חֲמָרָא וְסָיֵים מְסָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates Step 14 with a real event.
steps.raayaObject: That the protections do not work where there is a threat of כשפים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of a man who was harmed even though he was riding and wearing shoes

steps.title: Three things that should not pass between people
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a dog, a palm tree and a woman should not pass between two people, and people should not pass between two of them. Some add a pig, and some add a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three things should not go between people, and people should not go between them: a dog, a palm tree and a woman. Some say also a pig, and some say also a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about things that should not separate two people, and that two people should not separate. This carries on the theme of danger and כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש warned about passing between two palm trees. This ברייתא gives a wider list. It works both ways: these things should not come between two people, and a person should not walk between two of them. The 'יש אומרים' opinions add more items to the list.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'מְמַצְּעִין' and the word 'מִתְמַצְּעִין' work in opposite directions. The first means the thing passes between two people. The second means a person passes between two of these things. Both are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵין מְמַצְּעִין וְלֹא מִתְמַצְּעִין.
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Three things should not pass between, nor be passed between.
And these are they: a dog, a palm tree and a woman.
And some say: also a pig,
and some say: also a snake.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵין מְמַצְּעִין וְלֹא מִתְמַצְּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from spilled water to a ברייתא on related dangers, linked to the earlier palm tree material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dog, a palm tree and a woman (some add a pig, some a snake) should not pass between two people, nor should people pass between two of them.

steps.title: What if one of them already passed between two people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy there is if one of the listed things already passed between two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they do pass between them, what is the fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the ברייתא from the last step. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said these things should not pass between two people. It did not say what to do once it has happened. The גמרא now asks for a fix after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: they pass in the middle, between two people

phrases.english: And if they pass between them,
phrases.notes: Refers to the dog, palm tree, woman, and the others in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: what is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מְמַצְּעִין מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a remedy after the ברייתא in step 16 warned against passing between two people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a person should do if one of the dangerous things already passed between him and his companion.

steps.title: רב פפא: Recite verses that open and close with אל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says to recite a פסוק that begins with אל and end with a פסוק that ends with אל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He should begin with a verse that starts with 'אל' and end with a verse that ends with 'אל'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The person should say the פסוקים in במדבר that begin with 'אל' and end with 'אל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רשב"ם and the Sefaria note, these are the פסוקים in במדבר כ"ג:כ"ב–כ"ג, which say that no נחש or קסם works against ישראל. Saying them protects the person from the harm.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who gives the remedy

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
He should begin with 'God'
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק "אל מוציאם ממצרים" (במדבר כ"ג:כ"ב).

phrases.english: and conclude with 'God'.
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק "מה פעל אל" (במדבר כ"ג:כ"ג).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: נִפְתַּח בְּ״אֵל״ וְנַפְסֵיק בְּ״אֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Recite the פסוקים that begin and end with the word אל (במדבר כ"ג:כ"ב–כ"ג), which say that sorcery has no power over ישראל.

steps.title: Another option: recite a verse that opens and closes with לא
steps.stepSummary: Another option is to recite a פסוק that begins and ends with the word לא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, he should begin with 'לא' and end with 'לא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second option that works just as well. The person can say a פסוק that begins and ends with the word 'לא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the פסוק "לא איש אל ויכזב" (במדבר כ"ג:י"ט), which ends with "ולא יקימנה". It does not argue with the first answer. It only offers another way to fix the same problem.

phrases.english: Alternatively, he should begin with 'no'
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק "לא איש אל ויכזב" (במדבר כ"ג:י"ט).

phrases.english: and conclude with 'no'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, נִפְתַּח בְּ״לֹא״ וְנַפְסֵיק בְּ״לֹא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second option alongside רב פפא's remedy.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Recite במדבר כ"ג:י"ט, which begins and ends with לא.

steps.title: A menstruating woman passing between two men, and the remedy
steps.stepSummary: If a נדה passes between two men, she can cause one of them to die (at the start of her נדה) or cause a fight between them (at the end). The fix is the same אל verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two men that a נדה passes between: if it is the start of her נדה, she kills one of them. If it is the end of her נדה, she causes a fight between them. What is the fix? He should begin with 'אל' and end with 'אל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new danger: a נדה passing between two men. It then gives the same remedy of the אל פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger depends on timing. At the start of her נדה it can be deadly, and at the end it is weaker and only causes a fight. The remedy reuses רב פפא's answer from step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman in her menstrual period
the beginning of her menstrual period
the end of her menstrual period

phrases.english: These two men
between whom a menstruating woman passes,
if it is the beginning of her menstruation,
she kills one of them;
if it is the end of her menstruation,
she causes a fight between them.
What is his remedy?
He should begin with 'God' and conclude with 'God'.
phrases.notes: The same remedy as רב פפא's in step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי בֵּי תְרֵי דְּמַצַּעָא לְהוּ אִשָּׁה נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case of something passing between two people and applies the same remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה passing between two men endangers them: at the start of her period one may die, at the end there will be a quarrel. The remedy is the אל verses.

steps.title: Two women facing each other across a crossroads are doing witchcraft
steps.stepSummary: Two women sitting on opposite sides of a road at a crossroads, facing each other, are certainly doing כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two women who sit at a crossroads, one on this side of the path and one on the other side, facing each other, are certainly busy with כשפים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes a new danger: two women sitting across from each other at a crossroads. It says they are certainly doing כשפים, which sets up the remedies in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is again a case of passing between two people. This time the danger is not a natural harm but deliberate כשפים. The word ודאי means the גמרא treats it as a sure sign, not a doubt.

phrases.english: These two women
who sit at a crossroads,
one on this side of the path,
and one on the other side,
and they face each other,
they are certainly engaged in witchcraft.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תְּרֵי נְשֵׁי דְּיָתְבָן בְּפָרָשַׁת דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of dangers from passing between two people, now through כשפים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two women sitting facing each other across a road at a crossroads are presumed to be doing כשפים.

steps.title: Three remedies in order for passing the witches
steps.stepSummary: The fix comes in order: take another road; if there is none, hold hands with a companion and switch places; if alone, say a protective formula naming demons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the fix? If there is another road, he should take it. If there is no other road and there is another person with him, they should hold hands and switch places. If there is no other person, he should say: 'אגרת, אזלת, אסיא, בלוסיא are killed by arrows.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three remedies in order, from best to last resort. Each one is used only if the one before it is not possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best option is to avoid the danger completely. If he cannot, he and a friend change positions so the כשפים do not catch them. If he is alone, he says a formula that names the demons the witches call on and declares they are killed by arrows. This weakens the spell.

keyTerms.meaning: let them take each other's hands
are killed by arrows (part of the protective formula)

steps.whatToRemember: Every remedy here answers one question: 'מאי תקנתיה?' The answers are: for things passing between two people or a נדה, recite the אל (or לא) פסוקים. For witches at a crossroads, avoid the road, switch places with a friend, or say the formula.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
If there is another road,
he should go by it.
And if there is no other road,
if there is another person with him,
they should hold hands with each other
and switch places.
And if there is no other person,
he should say as follows:
'Iggeret, Azlat, Asiya, Belusiya','
phrases.notes: Names of demons that witches call on.

phrases.english: are killed by arrows.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ? אִי אִיכָּא דִּירְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא לֵיזִיל בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remedies for the danger described in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three remedies, each used only if the one before it is not possible: take another road; hold hands with a companion and switch places; say the formula naming the demons as killed by arrows.

steps.title: Meeting a woman coming up from her מצוה immersion
steps.stepSummary: If a man meets a woman coming up from a מצוה immersion, whoever has relations first is seized by a רוח זנונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man meets a woman just as she is coming up from her מצוה immersion: if he has relations first, a spirit of immorality grabs him. If she has relations first, a spirit of immorality grabs her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another danger to its list. This one comes from meeting a woman right after her טבילת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is fresh from her immersion and ready for her husband, so there is a charged state of desire. Whichever of the two acts on that desire first is overtaken by a רוח זנונים. The danger can strike either the man or the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה immersion, here a woman's immersion after her נדה period
A spirit of immorality, a strong drive toward forbidden relations
Goes first, acts before the other

phrases.english: One who meets a woman
at the time she comes up from a מצוה immersion,
if he goes first and has relations,
phrases.notes: Meaning he has relations with any woman before she has relations.

phrases.english: a spirit of immorality takes hold of him.
If she goes first and has relations,
a spirit of immorality takes hold of her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן דְּפָגַע בְּאִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another danger case in the same list as the נדה and כשפים cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever has relations first after this meeting is seized by a רוח זנונים.

steps.title: What is the fix?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the man can do to protect himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the man can protect himself from this danger. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier dangers on this list: first the danger, then the remedy. The question is short because the pattern is already familiar.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the remedy to the danger described in step 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to protect oneself from the רוח זנונים

steps.title: Say the verse about contempt poured on princes
steps.stepSummary: The fix is to say the פסוק 'שופך בוז על נדיבים ויתעם בתהו לא דרך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should say this: 'He pours contempt on princes and makes them wander in a wasteland where there is no path' (תהלים 107:40).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man should recite a specific פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of נדיבים being humbled and losing their way. The גמרא gives no reason; one possible understanding is that it is meant to push the harmful force away so that it loses its way and cannot reach him.

phrases.english: He should say this:
"He pours contempt upon princes
and makes them wander in a wasteland with no path."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24

steps.title: The valley of the shadow of death: sleeping in dangerous shadows
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads 'גיא צלמות' as a person sleeping in the shadow of a lone palm tree or in the shadow of the moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me'? This is someone who sleeps in the shadow of a lone palm tree, or in the shadow of the moon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains a famous פסוק from תהלים as describing two dangerous places to sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צלמות' contains the word 'צל', shadow, so the 'shadow of death' is read as a shadow that really is deadly. Two such shadows are named: a lone palm tree, where שדים are thought to rest, and the moon. A person in that spot who still does not fear is relying on ה׳ being with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The valley of the shadow of death

steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets up the two dangers that the rest of this passage limits and defines, one after the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is meant by what is written:
"Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ —
phrases.english: I will fear no evil, for You are with me"?
This is one who sleeps in the shadow of a lone palm tree,
and in the shadow of the moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new danger topic, introduced through a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping in the shadow of a lone palm tree or of the moon is dangerous.

steps.title: The lone palm tree is only dangerous without another tree's shadow
steps.stepSummary: The danger of a lone palm tree applies only when another tree's shadow does not also fall on the sleeper.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the shadow of a lone palm tree: we only said it is dangerous when the shadow of another tree does not fall on him. But if the shadow of another tree does fall on him, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the first danger from רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger comes from the tree being 'יחידי', alone. If the shadow of a second tree also falls on the sleeper, the tree is no longer really alone, so the danger goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when, a formula that limits a statement
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And about the shadow of a lone palm tree:
we only said this
when the shadow of another tree does not fall on him,
but if the shadow of another tree does fall on him,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְצֵל דֶּקֶל יְחִידִי — לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the lone palm tree danger named in step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second tree's shadow removes the danger of the lone palm tree.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא say 'in a courtyard'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא names the lone palm tree danger specifically in a courtyard. Under the plain case, the danger would exist in a field too, so why mention a courtyard?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא that teaches: One who sleeps in the shadow of a lone palm tree in a courtyard, or in the shadow of the moon, his blood is on his own head. What case is this? If you say the shadow of another tree does not fall on him, then the same would be true even in a field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that mentions 'in a courtyard' and asks why it chose that detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case were a lone tree with no second shadow, it would be dangerous anywhere, even in a field. So the word 'courtyard' must be teaching something new. This pushes us to find a case where a courtyard differs from a field.

keyTerms.meaning: That which was taught in a ברייתא
His blood is on his own head; he is responsible for his own harm

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack meant to cancel step 27. It is a question about why the ברייתא mentions a courtyard, and the answer adds a stricter rule for a courtyard.

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught in a ברייתא:
one who sleeps in the shadow of a lone palm tree in a courtyard,
and one who sleeps in the shadow of the moon,
his blood is on his own head.
What is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לֵימָא דְּלָא נָפֵל טוּלָּא דְּחַבְרֵיהּ עִילָּוֵיהּ,
phrases.english: If you say the shadow of another tree does not fall on him,
then even in a field too it would be dangerous!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limit of step 27 against the wording of a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's specific mention of 'in a courtyard'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is a tree with no second shadow, a field is just as dangerous, so the word 'courtyard' seems to add nothing.

steps.title: In a courtyard, a second shadow does not help
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean that in a courtyard the lone palm is dangerous even when another tree's shadow falls on him. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that in a courtyard it is dangerous even if the shadow of another tree falls on him? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the courtyard case is stricter than the field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The relief from step 27, where a second shadow removes the danger, works only in a field. In a courtyard, a lone palm tree stays dangerous even with another tree's shadow on the sleeper. 'שמע מינה' confirms that this reading is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from this?
Learn from it; yes, this is the conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: A lone palm tree in a field is dangerous only without a second tree's shadow. In a courtyard it is dangerous even with one.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
in a courtyard, even though
the shadow of another tree falls on him, it is dangerous.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 28 by showing that the courtyard case is a stricter one
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second-shadow exception applies only in a field. In a courtyard, the lone palm is always dangerous.

steps.title: The moon's shadow is only dangerous toward the west
steps.stepSummary: The moon's shadow is dangerous only when it falls to the west, not when it falls to the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the shadow of the moon: we only said it is dangerous when the shadow falls to the west. But when it falls to the east, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now narrows the second danger from רבי יצחק's statement, the shadow of the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of the month, the moon shines from the east, so its shadow falls to the west, and that is the dangerous time. At the start of the month, the moon shines from the west, so its shadow falls to the east, and that is harmless.
steps.whatToRemember: Both shadow dangers have been limited. The palm tree is dangerous when it is truly alone, or always in a courtyard. The moon is dangerous only when its shadow falls to the west.

phrases.english: And about the shadow of the moon:
we only said it is dangerous when the shadow is in the west,
phrases.notes: At the end of the month, when the moon shines from the east.

phrases.english: but when the shadow is in the east,
phrases.notes: At the start of the month, when the moon shines from the west.

phrases.english: we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְצִילָּהּ שֶׁל לְבָנָה — לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּמַעְרְבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second danger in step 26 after finishing with the palm tree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The moon's shadow is dangerous only when it falls westward.
